paper_title: Fuzzy-Based Thermal Management Scheme for 3D Chip Multicores with Stacked Caches

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 6(a)/(b): transient maximum temperature, mem2 and com2 program sets (with Section 4 setup on PDF pages 8-9)
scenario.description: Transient maximum temperature curves, 200-450 ms, comparing Baseline (DVFS), FLC (fuzzy control only) and FBTM (fuzzy control plus dynamic cache reconfiguration) while executing the mem2 and com2 multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 workload sets. The paper reports about 3 degrees C reduction and fluctuation within 0.5 degrees for FLC/FBTM versus up to 3.5 degrees for the baseline. No block coordinates, dimensions or per-block powers are published, so no floorplan can be extracted.
scenario.architecture: 3D-stacked NUCA cache: 4 cores in one core layer nearest the heat sink, with 3 stacked L2 cache layers. Each cache layer has 16 banks of 256 KB (CACTI), grouped into 4 cache zones of 4 banks, each zone sitting above one core. Each core has 32KB L1I and 32KB L1D. TSV-connected.
scenario.workload: Multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 sets of four applications each; Figure 6 shows mem2 (libquantum, lbm, GemsFDTD, art) and com2 (hmmer, mpeg_dec, astar). Power traces generated by gem5 and McPAT.
scenario.operating_point: Runtime-varying thermal threshold (per ref. 19); control step intervals; Algorithm 1 interval T = 2M clock cycles, allowed cache miss-rate degradation 3%; maximum temperature plotted roughly 75-81 degrees C over 200-450 ms. Ambient temperature, Vdd and frequency values are not given.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot grid-based thermal simulation, driven by gem5 (with Ruby memory model) performance traces and McPAT power traces. Cache bank capacity from CACTI. Super-core compact thermal model adapted from Zhou et al. (ref 9), Eqs. 1-2, PDF page 3.
original_setup.optimizer: No numerical optimizer. Dynamic cache reconfiguration (Algorithm 1) greedily gates cache banks, farthest from the heat sink first, using shadow-tag miss-rate prediction. Interval T = 2M clock cycles, allowed miss-rate degradation 3%.
original_setup.controller: Per-super-core fuzzy logic controller (FBTM). Inputs are the error e(n) between threshold and measured temperature (range [0,3]) and the temperature change rate (range [-1.5,1.5]). Each input has 3 triangular membership functions. 9 rules, mean-of-maxima defuzzification. Output is a normalized frequency ratio. FLC is the same controller without cache reconfiguration. Baseline is the DVFS technique of ref 18. Threshold is runtime-varying (ref 19).
original_setup.benchmark: Multiprogrammed SPEC CPU2006 workload sets of four applications each (com1, com2, med1, med2, mem1, mem2; Table 3, PDF page 9). Selected scenario is Figure 6 (PDF page 10): transient maximum temperature for mem2 and com2, 200-450 ms, comparing Baseline, FLC and FBTM.

thermal_observable.location: Transient maximum chip temperature over time (Figure 6a/b, mem2 and com2 sets). The plotted axis spans roughly 75-81 degC. The text reports about 3 degC reduction for FLC/FBTM versus baseline, with fluctuation within 0.5 degC versus up to 3.5 degC for the baseline. Exact per-curve numeric values are not tabulated.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the chip per control step, plotted as a time series over 200-450 ms. The 3 degC reduction is described as an average across the experiments (abstract). No single scalar is published for the selected scenario.

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D stacked architecture: one core layer plus three stacked L2 cache layers connected by TSVs, with a vertical super-core thermal model. A steady-state 2D single-layer floorplan cannot represent the inter-layer vertical coupling or the per-layer cache power gating.

Transient and controller-in-the-loop observable: the temperature trace depends on closed-loop fuzzy DVFS and runtime cache bank gating (a runtime-varying threshold). A static thermal solve cannot reproduce it.

No block geometry (x, y, width, height) or per-block power values are published. The paper gives only qualitative layout (Figure 1) and no per-block watts, so no complete floorplan or power set exists for this scenario.

Solver mismatch: the original uses HotSpot grid mode with gem5/McPAT power traces and the compact super-core model of Eqs. 1-2. The Studio solver is not the same toolchain, and the thermal resistances (Ramb, Rv), ambient temperature and package are not given.
Cooling and package parameters (heat sink, TIM, layer thicknesses, interposer or bonding layers) are not specified. Only the heat sink proximity of the core layer is stated.

missing_inputs: No paper-linked assets, repositories, supplementary data, code or config: the packet has an empty assets list and artifact_search_status is checked_no_links. The paper contains no availability-statement URLs for inputs.
Block names with x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m: no coordinates or dimensions are published; Figure 1 is qualitative only. Only the counts (4 cores, 16 banks per layer, 4 zones) are given.
Per-block power_rows (name and watts) for the mem2 or com2 scenario: none published. Total chip power is also not given, and it must not be split without a published rule.
Ambient temperature, Vdd, frequency levels, thermal resistances Ramb and Rv, thermal capacitance and Pgated values
HotSpot configuration: package, heat sink, layer thicknesses, material properties, grid resolution
Numeric thermal observable values for Figure 6 curves: only qualitative statements in the text, and digitization with uncertainty would be required
Runtime threshold temperature schedule (ref 19) and the fuzzy output membership parameters beyond Figure 5
Control step length and the McPAT/gem5 configuration files
